## Reproduced on

- roundhouse 08819dad (main, 2026-10-15). `src/analyze/harvest_return.rs` and `src/analyze/body/mod.rs` are
  unchanged on 00c83b2e (current main). Same output on e1e6b1be (2026-10-13). Spinel f3b89652d.

## Repro

`db/schema.rb`:

```ruby
ActiveRecord::Schema[8.0].define(version: 1) do
  create_table "widgets", force: :cascade do |t|
    t.string "name"
    t.json "prefs"
  end
end
```

`app/models/widget.rb`: `class Widget < ApplicationRecord; end`

`lib/prefs.rb` (`config.autoload_lib(ignore: %w[tasks])`):

```ruby
module Prefs
  def self.mode(widget)
    widget.prefs["mode"] || :basic
  end
end
```

`app/controllers/widgets_controller.rb`:

```ruby
class WidgetsController < ApplicationController
  def show
    widget = Widget.find(params[:id])
    render json: { mode: Prefs.mode(widget) }
  end
end
```

plus `config/routes.rb` (`get "widgets/:id", to: "widgets#show"`), `ApplicationRecord` and an
`ActionController::API` `ApplicationController`.

`roundhouse --target spinel -o out .` writes `out/app/models/prefs.rbs`:

```rbs
module Prefs
  def self.mode: (Widget widget) -> Symbol
end
```

A JSON column holds what the JSON holds: with `prefs = {"mode": "advanced"}` Rails answers `{"mode":"advanced"}`, a
String. The declaration says Symbol, and Spinel trusts it: on f3b89652d the build stops at
`incompatible types when returning type 'sp_RbVal' but 'sp_sym'` (Spinel's own gap, matz/spinel draft
`20261015-spinel-seeded-symbol-return-poly`), and once Spinel unboxes a seeded Symbol return the String's handle is
read as a Symbol id.

More of the same shape, each `-> Symbol`/`-> String` today:

```ruby
  def self.c(widget)
    widget.prefs || :en            # -> Symbol
  end

  def self.d(h)                    # called with JSON.parse(widget.name): (untyped h)
    h["lang"] || :en               # -> Symbol
  end

  def self.e(widget)
    widget.prefs["lang"] || "en"   # -> String
  end
```

while `widget.prefs` and `widget.prefs["lang"]` alone are `-> untyped`.

## Why it is wrong

`a || b` is `a`'s type (nil and false removed) joined with `b`'s. `BoolOp` in `src/analyze/body/mod.rs` does exactly
that and gives `untyped | Symbol`, and `render_union` in `src/emit/ruby/rbs.rs` renders any union with an `untyped`
variant as `untyped`. The variant is lost in between, in the harvested-return table.

## Root cause

`stabilize_untyped_return_oscillation` (`src/analyze/harvest_return.rs`, from 2bfebe6a / a8bd5cab) settles a return
that thrashes between `Configuration` and `Configuration | untyped` across fixpoint rounds by storing the concrete
core whenever the two writes differ only in top-level `untyped`/`Var` variants. Here neither write is concrete. A
trace of `insert_inferred_return` for `d` above (an `eprintln!` of the existing entry and the new type):

```
harvest d: existing=None                                   new=Union([Sym, Var { var: TyVar(0) }])
harvest d: existing=Some(Union([Sym, Var { var: TyVar(0) }])) new=Union([Sym, Untyped])
```

Both rounds carry an unknown variant (the parameter's pending `Var` first, `untyped` once it resolves), their cores
agree, and the second write stores the bare `Sym`; every later round then sees `Sym` against `Sym | untyped` and
keeps `Sym`. `c` traces the same way. That contradicts the rule the same file keeps for a first write
(`insert_preserves_first_write_of_gradual_union`: `String | untyped` is stored as is) and for a Nil core
(`var_nil_versus_untyped_nil_keeps_gradual_nil`): whether `h["k"] || :en` is declared `untyped` or `Symbol` depends
on whether its first round saw a `Var`.

## Proposed fix

Collapse to the core only when one side is concrete (the oscillation the function exists for). When both sides carry
an unknown variant and one of them is a real `untyped`, keep `core | untyped`, as the Nil branch already does:

```rust
    if existing.has_unknown_arm() && new.has_unknown_arm() && (has_untyped_arm(existing) || has_untyped_arm(new)) {
        return Some(body::union_of(core_e, Ty::Untyped));
    }
    Some(core_e)
}

/// True when `ty` is `untyped` or a union with a top-level `untyped` variant
/// (a `Var` variant is pending, not gradual, and does not count).
fn has_untyped_arm(ty: &Ty) -> bool {
    match ty {
        Ty::Union { variants } => variants.iter().any(|v| matches!(v, Ty::Untyped)),
        other => matches!(other, Ty::Untyped),
    }
}
```

with a unit test beside the existing ones (`Var | Symbol` then `untyped | Symbol`, both orders, then through
`insert_inferred_return` and back to `Var | Symbol`: the stored type stays `Symbol | untyped`).

Verified locally (release build of 08819dad + this change): every repro above declares `-> untyped`. On a
private ~600-file Rails app, 13 returns change, all from `-> T` / `-> T?` to `-> untyped`, all of the
`<untyped chain> || <literal>` or `cond ? <untyped> : <literal>` shape; no other emitted file changes except one
call site that had been lowered through the narrowed return. `cargo test --lib harvest_return`: 18 passed (the 17
existing and the new one). Not yet run through the full suite; the fixpoint
canaries (`fixpoint_check`) and the Campfire/lobsters compare jobs are the ones to watch, since the function was
added for a Campfire thrash. The longer-term version is #617's S2a (an `untyped` that carries its provenance), where
only a pending one would be absorbed.

## Duplicate check

`gh search issues --repo rubys/roundhouse` for "untyped ||", "stabilize harvested return", "I18n.locale=": #395
(open) is the same family, a multi-variant return narrowed to one variant in the emitted RBS, but its variants come from a
parameter typed by its call site, not from this stabilization. #617 (open) is the fixpoint RFC this touches.
